account: The Du et al. source text is present in the workspace and contains all needed evidence for the four required finding categories (claims, setup, limitations, and derived design constraints). However, the objective explicitly asks for two distinct derivation tasks: (b1) design constraints for the substrate and (b2) evaluation-replication requirements. These are separable analytical questions that can be answered independently from the same source file. Moreover, the acceptance condition demands both at least four anchored findings and at least three design/evaluation inferences; splitting the work ensures each part receives focused attention without duplicating the extraction effort. The children will work from the same frozen dossier and can independently cite the same file markers.

children.acceptance_condition: Returns at least four findings, each with the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), collectively covering claimed gains (factuality and reasoning), experimental setup (agents, rounds, tasks, consensus), and stated limitations. Each finding is a direct quote or close paraphrase from the Du file, and no design inference is labeled as a source claim.
children.expected_contribution: A set of anchored, source-grounded findings from Du et al. that the parent can cite verbatim in the final memo to fulfill D12 and support the reconciliation required by D11.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: This child uses only the Du source text, which is fully present in the workspace_documents. It does not require any output from the sibling child that derives design constraints; the extraction can be completed and checked without knowing the sibling's design conclusions.
children.objective: Extract from papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), at least four findings that cover: (a) the improvements in factuality and reasoning the paper claims for multiagent debate, (b) the experimental setup (number of agents, number of debate rounds, tasks used, and how consensus/final answer is reached), and (c) any limitations the authors state. Return each finding as a quote or close paraphrase with the exact page marker(s).
children.rationale: This child isolates the evidence-extraction portion of the node objective. It can be completed independently because the source file is fully enclosed and the required page markers are visible. The findings will be directly used by the parent to reconcile with null results and to inform the design constraints.
separator_facts: SC1: The evidentiary corpus is exactly seven extracted-text files under papers/text: dung-1995-argumentation.txt (Dung 1995, Artificial Intelligence 77), shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt (Shapiro et al., SSS 2011), lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt (Lorenz et al., PNAS 108, 2011), du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt (Du et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.14325), smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt (Smit et al. 2023, arXiv 2311.17371), zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt (Zhang et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.08788), choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt (Choi et al., Findings of ACL 2025).
SC2: Page boundaries in the extracted texts are marked with lines of the form `===== PDF PAGE N =====`, and these markers are the citation anchors required by D12/C3.

The corpus intentionally contains conflicting empirical conclusions: debate gains (Du et al. 2023) versus matched-compute null results and conformity findings (Smit et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2025; Choi et al. 2025; Lorenz et al. 2011); these must be preserved and reconciled, never hidden (C4).
Evidence is restricted to the seven workspace corpus files; no outside sources may be used (C2).
Source-supported claims must be clearly distinguished from design inferences in everything returned (D13).

children.acceptance_condition: Returns at least two design constraints and at least one evaluation-replication requirement, each explicitly labeled as 'design inference'. The design constraints identify substrate behaviors needed to retain Du et al.'s gains (e.g., multiple competing answers, cross-agent critique, iterative refinement, consensus convergence). The evaluation-replication requirement specifies the condition that replicates Du et al.'s setup (e.g., 3 agents, 2 rounds, same tasks, consensus prompt) and is falsifiable.
children.expected_contribution: A set of clearly labeled design inferences that the parent can use to argue why the proposed substrate captures the positive evidence from Du et al., and to specify the replication arm of the evaluation plan per D14.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: This child uses only the Du source text and the stable context facts. It does not need the sibling's extracted findings in a particular format; the inference can be derived directly from the source. Thus it can complete without waiting for the sibling's output.
children.objective: From the Du et al. source text, derive and return, each explicitly labeled as design inference: (b1) which debate behaviors a shared question/answer substrate must capture to retain the reported gains, and (b2) what an evaluation condition replicating the paper's setup would require. This includes at least two design constraints and at least one evaluation-replication requirement.
children.rationale: This child isolates the design-inference portion of the node objective. It is analytically independent from the evidence-extraction child because it derives conclusions from the same source file but does not need the extracted findings pre-formatted; it can independently read the source and produce its inferences. The parent will combine the extracted evidence with these inferences.

decidability.account: The full source text is enclosed in the workspace_documents, so all cited claims are directly checkable. The node's acceptance condition is substantive but not merely mechanical: it requires human judgment on whether the extracted findings are faithful and whether the design inferences are clearly labeled and distinct from source claims. However, this judgment can be fully made from the provided source and the design inference does not depend on any sibling's future output. Thus the node is locally decidable.

synthesis_contract.acceptance_condition: The combined output from the two children provides at least four anchored findings covering the four categories, at least two design constraints, at least one evaluation-replication requirement, and the entire set is labeled to distinguish source claims from design inferences. The synthesis is faithful to Du et al. and ready to be used by the parent for D4, D11, D12, D13, and D14.
synthesis_contract.conflict_policy: If the two children's outputs disagree on the interpretation of a specific page or claim, the parent will re-check the original source text at the cited marker(s) and favor the reading that is closest to the literal wording of the paper. Design inferences that conflict with each other will be flagged as alternative hypotheses for the reconciliation section, not silently resolved.
synthesis_contract.parent_question: What does Du et al. 2023 claim about multiagent debate gains, what experimental setup produced them, what limitations do the authors state, and what design and evaluation implications follow for a shared question/answer substrate?
required_contributions: At least four anchored findings from Du et al. covering claimed gains, experimental setup (agents, rounds, tasks, consensus mechanism), and stated limitations, each with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
At least two design constraints for the substrate, explicitly labeled as design inference, identifying debate behaviors the substrate must capture.
At least one evaluation-replication requirement, explicitly labeled as design inference, specifying a condition that replicates Du et al.'s setup.
Clear labeling distinguishing source-supported findings from design inferences.
